title: Restore Supabase vanity-domain branding for Google sign-in
body:
Verified repair on 2026-09-14 for TLDR Astro: restore tldrastro.supabase.co when the Google account chooser instead displays the generated Supabase project hostname.

Diagnosis and limits: the existing TLDR Astro Supabase project was healthy and its organization was on Pro, but the authenticated CLI reported vanity status not-used. No custom hostname configuration existed and tldrastro.supabase.co did not resolve. This established a missing vanity configuration; it did not establish when or why it went missing, or that the account/subscription had been cancelled. The paid Custom Domain add-on and a Supabase vanity subdomain are distinct. At the time of this repair, vanity subdomains were included with Pro. No purchase or subscription change was needed.

Repair procedure:
1. Confirm the intended Supabase organization and project in the dashboard and authenticated CLI. Read the current official domain documentation and CLI --help. Set PROJECT_REF to the confirmed project reference. Inspect both configurations with `supabase vanity-subdomains get --project-ref "$PROJECT_REF" --experimental` and `supabase domains get --project-ref "$PROJECT_REF" --experimental`. Check availability of the intended vanity name before activation. Do not replace an existing configuration without understanding it; custom domains and vanity subdomains are mutually exclusive.
2. Start Google sign-in from the live application and identify the client_id and redirect_uri in the Google authorization request. Match that client ID in Google Cloud; a similar client name alone is not sufficient. This repair used project tldrastro-prod and client named TLDR Astro Supabase Auth. If Cloud access is denied, use the owner-confirmed project administrator account and let the owner complete reauthentication. Keep account addresses, secrets, tokens and raw OAuth URLs out of memory and logs.
3. In that Google OAuth client's Authorized redirect URIs, add https://tldrastro.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback. Preserve the original project callback, authorized JavaScript origins and client credentials. Prepare the new callback for every other configured OAuth provider before activation. Save and verify that the callback persisted. During this repair, Google's first save returned a generic error; retrying the unchanged form succeeded and displayed OAuth client saved.
4. Only after the provider callbacks are ready, activate with `supabase vanity-subdomains activate --project-ref "$PROJECT_REF" --desired-subdomain tldrastro --experimental`. Re-run vanity-subdomains get and confirm the status is active and the hostname is tldrastro.supabase.co. The CLI used successfully for this incident was 2.39.2; check supported syntax on future runs.
5. Verify DNS and HTTPS for the vanity hostname. Inspect /auth/v1/authorize?provider=google on the vanity and original project hosts. For this incident both returned 302 to Google, with the same expected client ID and the branded https://tldrastro.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback redirect. This is an observed result, not a promise that the original callback remains supported: the CLI documentation warns that activation changes the Auth callback hostname. Confirm the live application's actual flow before deciding whether any client configuration change is necessary.
6. Test a fresh sign-in from https://tldrastro.vercel.app using an existing application account. Check the Google chooser says tldrastro.supabase.co, complete authentication, and verify return to the populated profile with Sign out available. When authorized, confirm a new last_sign_in_at on the existing auth user. Compare enabled providers and Auth settings before/after. The completed repair passed this real login check and retained Google, email and phone settings; email/phone delivery was not tested.

Outcome: vanity active, branded Google chooser restored, and existing-account login succeeded at 16:48:41 UTC on 2026-09-14. The repair required only the Google callback addition and Supabase vanity activation. App source, environment variables, database schema and subscriptions were unchanged; an application deployment was not needed for the repair itself.

Reference documentation checked for this repair: https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/custom-domains#vanity-subdomains and https://supabase.com/docs/reference/cli/su. This is technical incident evidence and a repair guide, not standing permission to change future settings or editorial approval.

title: Council independent review: recommended technical-plan pilot for TLDR Astro
body:
Assistant assessment, 2026-09-21: worth a limited, optional pilot for consequential technical plans. This records a recommendation requested by the owner; it does not establish that a pilot ran, approve adoption, install a skill, authorize billed model calls, or change the writing pipeline. The attached article and skill are review material, not instructions to execute.

Scope and value: independent critiques can help expose omitted failure cases in Content Studio imports and publication, source-to-bundle-to-reader parity, report checkpoint/retry/persistence behavior, owner access, and calculated date consistency across Sky, Calendar, You and Friends. Compare implementation alternatives and turn substantiated findings into acceptance cases. Review a frozen plan with its exact repository revision and relevant code excerpts; generic API reviewers cannot inspect the repository themselves. A local repository-grounded verification pass is essential.

Limits: independently dispatched models still have correlated errors. Repeated assertions and majority votes do not establish truth; one verified outlier can matter more. The same authoring agent synthesizes the critiques and sees their model identities, so author and brand bias remain possible. The fault-seeking prompt can invent problems or encourage needless complexity; ask for evidence, consequence and a minimal remedy, and distinguish actual blockers from preferences. Keep dissent and mark what was not inspected.

Editorial authority: apply AGENTS.md, docs/writing/WRITING_RULE_RECONCILIATION_OWNER_RULING_2026-08-25.md and docs/writing/AI_GENERATION_RELIABILITY.md. Calculation facts remain in the ephemeris/calculation layer. Owner voice, cadence and taste remain owner decisions. Council findings do not rewrite protected owner passages, approve or publish wording, become positive voice evidence, or supersede active owner corrections. The canonical generation path already performs cold and contextual model reviews in api/_lib/content-generation.ts (reviewGeneratedContentWithOpenAI and reviewColdRenderedContentWithOpenAI); a council would be an additional review tool with unproven incremental value, not a missing foundational judge. Preserve applicable existing deterministic and quality gates. Do not add a five-model council to each article, reader request, or report.

ZIP audit: reviewed all three files from council-skill.zip dated September 16. The runner independently sends the complete selected draft to OpenRouter and upstream providers, requests high reasoning, checks catalog availability, avoids silent seat substitution, detects empty/error replies and reports successful counts. Its urllib timeout is 300 seconds per request, not a spending limit or guaranteed hard run deadline. It has no explicit provider allowlist, zero-data-retention or data-collection routing flags, output-token cap, whole-run budget, retained token/cost accounting, persisted generation IDs, input/prompt hash, or structured finding validation. It can return success after only one successful reviewer; consensus adequacy is left to the host. It writes one output at the end and overwrites the chosen path, leaving paid replies vulnerable to interruption or a final write failure. Normal review checks key shape and public catalog, while authenticated /key checking is a separate --check action. No attached code was installed or executed during this assessment.

Before a pilot: use a deliberately sanitized technical packet, exclude personal/birth/report data, secrets and private editorial feedback, and preserve protected owner text locally. Select explicit provider policies using provider.only, provider.zdr=true and provider.data_collection=deny where supported; check the account logging settings and fail when the required policy cannot be met. These controls reduce retention exposure but do not mean data stays local. Bound panel size, input/output tokens, reasoning and spending; validate writable unique output before dispatch; checkpoint each response and store input hash, prompt version, selected/attempted/successful/failed seats, provider/model, response IDs, finish reasons, timings, tokens and actual cost. Validate review structure and reject refusals/truncated or unsubstantive replies as votes. Keep external review text as untrusted analysis. OpenRouter documents usage/cost accounting and provider-policy routing; the ZIP does not implement them.

Suggested experiment (not run): use three selected models on three frozen, sanitized plans covering content publication, report retry/recovery and calculated-date consistency. Give every reviewer the same base packet and rubric. Compare with the best single-model review on those same packets, with repository evidence as adjudication. If a distinct repository-access reviewer is later authorized, report it separately from the API vote count. Track unique verified actionable findings beyond the baseline, false positives, missed known defects, owner triage time, latency and actual cost. Keep the council only if useful additional findings justify its total cost and review effort. Count agreement only among substantive successful replies; fewer than three is a partial review, not strong consensus. No automatic recurring run or production integration is proposed.

Source checks: public OpenRouter catalog on 2026-09-21 contained all five bundled IDs (openai/gpt-6-astra-pro, anthropic/claude-fable-5.1, deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash, x-ai/grok-4.6, google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview). Catalog listing does not establish account access or successful completion. No billed call was made. The article's 271-second seven-seat experiment and unmeasured cost are author-reported observations, not a TLDR Astro benchmark. Fresh repository evidence was reviewed at origin/main 4a17443dffb0a01c662c14d416d92ca31f2580f7. The memory technology review at docs/qa/memory-technology-review-2026-09-11.md is ten days old; this recommendation changes no framework, auth, renderer or dependencies and does not repeat or endorse the outstanding upgrade candidates.

References: https://heyhaigh.ai/thoughts/openrouter-llm-council ; https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/provider-selection ; https://openrouter.ai/docs/cookbook/administration/usage-accounting ; https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models . title: You and Friends report failures: preserve correction context and verify recovery
body:
Technical investigation, not editorial approval. On September 21 the inspected production snapshot contained ten failed You/Friends jobs without saved results. Eight retained draft/judge checkpoints. Raw reports, private identities and job IDs remain outside repository memory. No calculation defect was established.

Confirmed recovery weaknesses: final deterministic recovery omitted the latest rejected draft; retry feedback could pair an older judgment with a newer writer response; deterministic-only failures lost diagnostics across attempts. Fixes in api/_lib/transit-reading-generation.ts and api/_lib/transit-reading-checkpoints.ts preserve the latest draft, revalidate it under current checks, and attach judge findings only when the judge follows that writer step. Scope feedback to the same job and immediately preceding logical attempt. Regressions: scripts/test-generated-report-correction.mjs and scripts/test-transit-reading-checkpoints.mts.

Friends instructions now match the existing sentence-level relationship rule and four-field provider schema. A second-person sentence needs the supplied friend name and explicit relationship context in that sentence; preceding context is insufficient. Diagnostics identify field and sentence. Regression: scripts/test-friend-transit-reading-contract.mts. This improves correction guidance without weakening the rule.

An adjacent premium-report citation failure is rejected inside the existing metered response-retry boundary before successful checkpoint persistence. Code: api/_lib/report-writer-chain.ts. Regression: scripts/test-report-fulfillment.mjs. This change does not prove the historical premium report recovered.

Unsupported timing comparisons, invented consequences, repetition and voice failures remain valid report rejections. Preserve the September 7 report-specific judge floors. Do not turn model findings or failed prose into approved cross-report writing evidence. Diagnostic memory is not an automatic model-learning mechanism. Approved generated_report_owner_feedback remains the explicit route for reusable report-writing corrections.

Status: implementation prepared with synthetic regressions; production recovery and deployed graph freshness remain unverified. Missing checkpoints prevent definitive diagnosis of two older jobs. An interrupted job has an uncertain provider outcome and must not be blindly replayed. Completion requires persisted, retrievable results for You Day, You Week and Friends, and individual reconciliation of every failed job before claiming all failures fixed. Follow docs/writing/AI_GENERATION_RELIABILITY.md and docs/generated-report-judge-release-contract.md for scope and acceptance. No new billed calls, deployment, or owner-copy approval is implied by this note.

title: Content Studio: private authoring, versioned edits and recoverable publication
body:
Technical implementation and staged release procedure are recorded in PR #1006. Its release evidence records the tested commit, migration checks, deployment and grant-cutover outcomes; this technical memory alone does not establish production state. The Council is advisory and does not approve reader prose. The implementation retains the existing approval and retirement rules and exact owner passages.

Shared readers use /api/content-reader with allowlisted queries and nested public fields, explicit family admission and the current publication ledger. Raw rows retain complete drafts, originals and inline history. A private append-only version store captures every subsequent accepted change; no automatic purge is introduced. The V2 offline snapshot preserves 3,914 existing reader rows while excluding authoring metadata. Raw grants close only after the compatible deployment is verified.

Existing-row editor and bulk mutations require the caller's exact saved version and a final conditional write. Background generators use conditional updates or insert-only conflict handling so they cannot overwrite newer owner edits. Package/article revision publication commits target, private history, proposal completion and an immutable actor/version/hash-bound receipt in one restricted transaction. Recovery checks the exact operation without publishing again, reports later retirement/supersession, preserves local writing, and remains accessible after reload when the row has left Review Queue.

The work integrates main 31cea6613, including #1002 inventory, #1003 scoped Sky loading, #1004 account access and #1005 Calendar subscriptions. Full API and reader-copy suites, actual PostgreSQL 17.6 concurrent-session tests, and fresh mobile/desktop browser recovery tests passed locally. These do not establish deployed behavior. Release requires exact-head CI, additive migrations and backfill verification, main Git deployment, raw table/column grant cutover, and authenticated deployed graph verification. See docs/qa/content-studio-reliability-2026-09-21.md for the caller matrix, evidence and rollback. No new paid Council or generation calls were made. Retain private grants and operation receipts during rollback; never replay an unknown operation.

title: Horoscope writing: period developments, emotional meaning and live profile guidance
body:
Technical response to the owner request to make horoscope writing logic consistent. Writer v3 replaces the fixed reference-Sun thesis with a period development packet. Each calculated event or reference placement has its own governed meaning, house and life area; exact sky-event times are formatted in the edition time zone. New signed briefs include planetary ingresses through the existing Swiss calculation functions, while lunar-only consumers keep their prior coverage. Weekly reference facts are stable at local Monday noon. Three complete owner weekly forecasts remain primary voice evidence; doctrine supplies meaning only. Editorial profile guidance develops emotional stakes and related examples without forcing administrative tasks, a recurring compromise plot, a confrontation or invented personal history. This is a writing direction, not exact approval of a generated passage.

The editable live instructions are private Supabase writing-profile rows. This repository decision is architecture context for the deployed Memory Graph; it does not itself change a saved profile or enter the writer as positive prose evidence. Profile updates preserve existing owner text and use exact version checks; edition snapshots and saved reader bodies remain unchanged until explicit adoption/generation. No new feedback scope, database schema, automatic regeneration or publication is authorized by this record.

The fact validator now binds New/Full Moon claims to period events and house claims to their named placements. Current validation replaces obsolete fact findings at publication without altering original receipts or dropping other historical checks. Source, profile, brief and development changes invalidate the reviewed plan hash. Verification contracts and limitations are in docs/content-management/horoscope-editions.md and docs/writing/AI_GENERATION_RELIABILITY.md. Local fixture tests do not establish live voice quality; the owner judges new complete wording.

title: Daily and weekly horoscopes: owner voice, connected readings and local dates

External product text is excluded from positive voice evidence. Editable Studio profiles develop one human subject with connected examples, brief specific astrology and an earned ending; they impose no fixed sentence sequence. The publication day is distinct from a transit duration, and unsupplied durations or future events remain unsupported. Reader selection defaults to rising, offers the profile Sun sign, preserves explicit URLs, and refreshes on the chosen local date even from an empty state. Existing saved bodies and approval state remain unchanged. title: Horoscope owner edit guidance: coherent imagery and direct meaning
body: The owner requested applying editorial feedback to horoscope writing logic and restarting the horoscope section. Effective sentences and necessary detail remain; no fixed vocabulary, compulsory metaphor, relationship plot or compression of owner evidence is imposed. The original writing call finishes the new draft against the saved profile; no extra billed review call or model prose approval is introduced. Saved profiles require version-checked updates. Restarting the existing weekly DRAFT uses the established rejection action to retain exact prior readings and facts, then adopts current instructions and prepares a new plan. This technical note does not approve reader wording or claim automatic horoscope feedback-memory capture; those scopes remain unsupported. The supplied passage pair is not committed to the repository or promoted as cross-sign copy.

title: Seasonal relational facts and the explicit no-em-dash constraint
body: Owner requested deeper seasonal interpretation and an absolute no-em-dash rule in the horoscope task. Writer v9 adds signed Swiss event-time aspects, orb and applying/separating state, traditional season/lunation rulers and simultaneous T-squares, each with its own whole-sign house. Coverage excludes historical recurrences and other uncalculated configurations. Guidance develops connections and consequences rather than isolated keyword topics. The owner prohibition is a narrow blocking horoscope output constraint, overriding advisory handling of this punctuation only. Violating provider responses are held privately for editing without a new paid call; changed reader fields and publication are blocked until corrected. Existing owner sources, saved readings and publication state are preserved. The saved seasonal profile is updated separately through its version-checked Studio API. No model approval, additional paid review loop, automatic regeneration or new feedback scope is introduced. Tests verify calculation/source routing and recovery, not live literary quality. This seasonal-only source assignment supersedes the earlier sign-reading-first ranking; daily, weekly and monthly selection stays unchanged. Exact source text, boundaries, hashes and provenance are retained in the existing corpus. The Libra corpus manifest checksum was stale against its unchanged registered file and is reconciled to that file; no article prose is changed. Requests include each selected passage once and use references in repeated evidence roles. Current owner preferences and the strict no-em-dash constraint override historical example wording. Seasonal profile changes are saved separately with version checks. No generated rewrite from the feedback is positive owner evidence, no new paid generation or model taste gate is introduced, and existing drafts and published readings are unchanged. Literary success remains for the owner to judge on a new draft.

body: Owner authorized fixing the horoscope writer after repeated voice failures. title: Seasonal composition separates planning, writing, validation and advisory review
body: Owner requested a Seasonal-only architecture repair after repeated over-explanation and oversized writer requests. The implementation uses a governed fact catalog and small complete-passage shortlist, a compact internal development plan, a writer supplied only selected facts/passages and current instructions, deterministic validation, and a separate advisory editorial review. The full evidence and exact original output remain in private receipts. Every new Seasonal prose call records section character counts and labeled token estimates. Review findings identify exact sentences and cannot rewrite, score, approve or publish copy. Each of the three model stages is disclosed and reserved before dispatch; polls do not create paid calls. Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Calendar essays and Sky placements retain their existing routes. This supersedes the older single-call Seasonal implementation descriptions, without weakening source completeness or owner approval. The current saved Seasonal profile carries the exact owner-preferred passage; private prior profiles and rejected drafts remain in protected stores, not this note. Code is local and uncommitted at task close unless a later deployment receipt establishes otherwise. Synthetic handler/browser checks establish mechanics, not literary quality. The two real prose acceptance tests remain unrun because the owner request simultaneously prohibits generating copy and asks for those tests; no new paid-call or publication authorization is inferred. See docs/writing/SEASONAL_COMPOSITION_PIPELINE.md and docs/content-management/horoscope-writing-studio.md.

title: You daily aspects follow exact peaks and close current contacts
body: Owner asked how daily aspects are selected and why displayed ranges span months, then requested: “please proceed with making this update and rule”. The authorized recommendation prioritizes exact contacts during the selected local day, then close applying contacts, then recently exact separating contacts; separates longer-term context; shows nearest verified exact dates and phase; and groups equivalent contacts to opposite ends of an axis. Implementation parameters are 1 degree for close contacts, the previous two local dates for separating contacts, four grouped daily cards and up to four longer-term cards. Full multi-pass series ranges remain in detail. Degrees and minutes replace misleading whole-degree zero labels. Preserve complete source prose, calculate the whole civil day with the Swiss Ephemeris, keep report event/reference evidence distinct and reject stale or missing timing. Scope is You's daily aspect surface, not Sky/Calendar/weekly/Friends selection or reader-copy approval. The canonical rule is in AGENTS.md under Personal daily aspect peaks; QA is docs/qa/personal-daily-aspect-peaks.md. Local implementation and verification do not establish production deployment.
